title: Characterizing a Memory Allocator at Warehouse Scale
problem: Memory allocation constitutes a substantial component of warehouse-scale computation costs and performance overhead. Understanding memory allocator behavior and bottlenecks at datacenter scale is critical for optimization.
motivation: Optimizing memory allocators reduces datacenter operational costs and improves application performance significantly.
method: The researchers measured how memory allocators actually perform by profiling production datacenter workloads. They tracked memory request patterns, identified bottlenecks from processes competing for resources (contention), measured memory fragmentation (wasted gaps between allocated blocks), and quantified the performance impact across different applications.
key_novelty: The paper reveals how memory allocators actually behave in real production datacenters by systematically measuring warehouse-scale workloads and identifying their performance impact.
contributions: Empirical characterization of memory allocator behavior at warehouse scale
Identification of performance bottlenecks and inefficiencies
Quantification of memory allocation overhead and datacenter tax

metrics.other: memory allocation overhead, datacenter cost reduction

limitations: Specific limitations not discussed in abstract.
